The reclaimed lands will be topographically lower and much smoother than now exists and will lack the present variety due to changes in the kind of surface and near-surface soil and rock. The smoother reclaimed surface may be more productive over the long-term if used for farming rather than the intended reclamation for stock-forage purposes.
Fish and Wildlife
The effects on fish and wildlife will range from minor harrassment to total destruction of their habitat, resulting in displacement or possible loss of life. Reclamation should preclude total habitat disruption throughout the life of the project, but substantial areas (2,744 and 4,011 acres at the low and high levels of production after 1989) will be unavailable at any given time period. In addition, many wildlife habitat attributes will be permanently lost due to loss of plant cover diversity and the removal of rock ledges and outcrops. Permanent loss of some water sources may result in decreased carrying capacity, or redistribution of some species.
Success of reclamation efforts will determine the long-term productivity of fish and wildlife. When the land is reclaimed for stock-forage purposes, some species of wildlife will return and use the land. If different food, cover, or nesting conditions are produced, new species may become established; in any case, the existing balance of species will probably not exist.
